items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Thad Jones, Snooky Young, Sonny Cohn and Lenny Johnson were in the trumpet section and they were making up riffs behind me that had me blowing my buns off.

ctx.x: Basie asked me who I wanted to come out front with me to assist in the rounds of solos. I was so excited that I couldn't answer. I had been an admirer of Basie's style of band since the first time I heard it on radio in Egypt in 1939. I had also heard his recording of "Blue and Sentimental" in a movie house in Egypt and didn't know until years later that it was Basie and the big tone of Herchel Evans on tenor and Prez on clarinet. I never saw Herchel because he died before I returned to the States. Basie had a…

And now, here I was on the verge of being accompanied by my favorite big band and that's all that I could think of. I should have asked for Budd Johnson and Quentin "Butter" Jackson to come out front with me because we were buddies and they had recorded with me the year before when both of them were in France with the Quincy Jones orchestra. I didn't speak up quick enough, so Basie motioned for Frank Wess and Frank Foster to come forward. Wess played flute and Foster tenor on the two numbers I did with the band…

The two numbers I did with Basie had more effect on the public and meant more to my prestige than any amount of numbers that I probably could have done with My Can. There was no broadcast of the festival that night but the radio who had recorded it for further broadcast made a copy of it and I happened to be able to get one which I shall always cherish.
